method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, proof reverse paraphrase, exact formula, macro, token and identifier comparison; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Soundness of the sequent-calculus identity rules, including identity initial sequents and semantic substitution in the equality inference.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section states that LK extended with identity initial sequents and identity rules is sound. The identity initial sequent with a closed term t is valid in every structure because t equals itself and contains no variables.
samples.checks: The soundness proposition, identity token, initial-sequent formula, closed-term condition, structure quantifier and satisfaction formula remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For the equality inference from A(t1) to A(t2), the premise contains equality t1=t2 and A(t1) on the right, while the conclusion contains A(t2). To prove validity, fix a structure satisfying the equality and the left context; then either an existing right-side formula is satisfied or A(t2) must be shown.
samples.checks: The premise and conclusion sequents, equality and context formulas, structure token, validity condition and right-side alternatives are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The induction hypothesis yields either a right-context witness or A(t1). In the second case, assign x the value of t1, transfer sentence satisfaction to A(x), use equality to identify the value of t2, transfer back to A(t2), and conclude sentence satisfaction of A(t2).
samples.checks: The two induction cases, variable assignment, value equations, assignment-update macro, all three semantic references and every satisfaction formula remain unchanged.

source_observations: The frozen upstream source gives the identity-rule soundness argument; no upstream defect or correction was identified in this unit.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
